Subject: Aquila Systems -- activation safelist + rollback guardrails (need prioritization)

Team —

Quick context: Aquila (large enterprise, SF-based) is at the final stage of legal/fin-proc and has indicated they will sign our Dedicated contract if we commit to two activation safety items: a deploy-time "output safelist" enforcement for PII/SSN/financial ids and an automated rollback guardrail that can flip traffic to a safe model variant within seconds if the canary crosses a quality or safety threshold.

They surfaced this during yesterday's legal+security call and Procurement asked me to get a prioritized internal ask into Product/Eng so they can decide on an internal approval acceleration and commit date. Attached is the latest SOW and a short acceptance criteria sheet they sent.

Asks:
- Can Product/Eng confirm whether this is feasible to scope as a prioritized engineering workstream with a tentative ETA?
- If prioritization is required for an earlier ship, what is the realistic earliest EAP (early access) window we can promise?
- What are the tradeoffs (perf/cost/SLA) we should flag to the customer now?

Notes: Aquila's legal explicitly required a documented rollback plan and said they will withhold final sign-off until they see a technical plan. They're also asking for an operational playbook for canary monitoring (error thresholds, PSO contact, rollback runbook).

Attachments: Aquila_SOW_v3.pdf, activation_acceptance_criteria.xlsx, fallback_policy_draft.md

Thanks Ben — good summary.

High-level reaction from Product: the ask breaks down into two capabilities:
1) Output safelist enforcement (policy layer) — validate/strip/replace model tokens that match disallowed patterns at generation time; optional learning/inference-time blocking.
2) Fast rollback/fallback routing — automated routing policy that flips from a primary model to an approved "safe" variant when monitoring rules trigger.

Questions for clarity (need answers to scope properly):
- How strict is Aquila on false positives in the safelist? Do they prefer aggressive blocking or allow hashed tokens for post-hoc review?
- Does the rollback need to be global (all tenants) or per-tenant binding?
- Are they requiring an on-demand manual rollback button in the Console in addition to automatic traffic fencing?

Initial Product proposal:
- MVP: a per-tenant safelist config + server-side enforcement hook (no UI) + an API-driven rollback switch that can be called by our ops playbook.
- Stretch: Console controls, progressive canary with automated metrics-based rollback, and an audit trail export for compliance.

We need Eng to weigh in on timeline. Dev / Jordan — can you flag feasibility and rough ETA (MVP vs stretch) and call out any infra risks (KV cache invalidation, latency cliff, billing implications)?

—Kimberly

On Fri, Jun 5, 2026 at 11:03 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Initial Product proposal:
> - MVP: a per-tenant safelist config + server-side enforcement hook (no UI) + an API-driven rollback switch that can be called by our ops playbook.

High-level Eng feasibility: doable, but with clear resource and design choices. TL;DR timelines below — details after.

Estimated timelines (if pulled into priority):
- Option A (accelerated): MVP in ~6 weeks (2 sprints) if we dedicate a small focused squad (1 backend, 1 infra, 1 QA, 0.5 frontend for minimal admin API). This would be server-only controls + audit logs + a simple API-based rollback endpoint.
- Option B (standard): MVP in ~12 weeks (4 sprints) if squad availability is normal; includes some integration testing with Dedicated runtime.
- Stretch (ui + progressive canary automation): additional 6-8 weeks after MVP.

Engineering caveats / tradeoffs:
- Safelist enforcement must live in the token post-processing stage. We can implement pattern-based blocking and allowlist overrides. However, aggressive blocking increases token processing time by ~10-25ms per request depending on sequence length — expect modest P99 latency impact.
- Rollback flip: can be implemented via routing table update + model alias pointing. We can achieve sub-5s failover if we accept eventual consistency across distributed routers; strict sub-second atomic flip needs additional coordination and may add complexity (and risk).
- Auditability: we can log masked examples and policy hits to the audit pipeline; retention and export will affect storage costs.

Blocking asks from Eng to Sales/Product:
- Final confirmation of safelist strictness and whether hashed sample retention is acceptable.
- A prioritized acceptance criteria doc from Aquila (we have the attachment but need line-by-line sign-off on thresholds).
- Budget/commit: does Sales have flexibility to convert this work into a funded engineering uplift (contract addendum)? If not, we need to slot into existing roadmap windows.

I opened an initial ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9843 (outline + tech notes). I'll add more details and perf numbers there.
